about: C-356. A lexicon of signs for the dream journal, distilled by hand from the four in-game books (THE SUBTLE LAYER, THE HERMETIC LAYER, THE EUDAIMON LAYER and THE UNITY BOOK) so a small local model can read a dream or a journal entry in their terms without carrying the books whole. Every word is DRAFT. The principles are always sent with a reading; a symbol is retrieved when one of its keys is found in the entry, and its readings are offered as possibilities, never verdicts.

principles.line: Every image may be a lean, not a fact: something not yet settled. Note it with the day and the centre it touched, and let the log, not the calm, decide later.
Imagination tends to arrive with argument and worry; a read tends to arrive quiet and whole. If an image makes you more still, it may be worth writing down.
A shadow is a part no longer watched, loyal to an old instruction. A dream may bring one forward so it can be seen, not fought.
The body balances through seven centres, root to crown. An image may point to the centre asking for care: too closed, too open, or in balance.
As above, so below: a small image in a dream may echo a large pattern in the day, and the reverse. Ask from which fold you are looking.
Every change runs through the Work: black, white, dawn, red. An ending in a dream may be the first colour of a turning, not a ruin.
Words are spells and nouns are verbs told to hold still. A feeling named in a dream as a thing may be read again as something you are doing.
What has touched stays touched. Objects and companions in a dream may stand for the one bound to them, and what is done to one reaches the other.
Read from the palm, nothing in the dream was against you. Ask what each image would give you, if it were a gift.
The old word for a daemon meant the one who deals the portions. A dream may show how your share is being dealt, and how you are keeping it.
An ending read from the dawn side is often a rest, not a crash: an old shape allowed to stop. A verb is a noun allowed to move again.
The shadows and the light are two halves of one horizon. A dark image and a bright one may be one motion read from two sides; neither is a verdict.
Every shadow sits under its virtue the way a root sits under a tree: thrall under circle, devouring under measure, binding under offering, slumber under vigil.
Reason and instinct are two eyes, and depth needs both. Read the dream once for its parts and once for the shape the parts were making.
One loop runs at every size: in, read, out, back. A dream that repeats may be a loop asking to be read more kindly the next time round.

readings.reading: Water often comes with feeling, the sacral centre's ground. Calm water may point to a feeling held in balance; a flood may ask whether a want is steering every turn.
Read from the dawn side, a feeling named in the past tense is already water going by. Moving water may show something you were, not something you are.
A boulder is a very slow river: what looks fixed may be a process running slowly. Water in a dream may ask what you have mistaken for stone.
In the craft, fire is the voltage of rage, and it steers toward fire-shaped outcomes, including the ones you stand in. A blaze may ask where strong feeling has no address.
The Work changes a thing the way fire does: you can watch it. Burning was the old emblem of lust, and distilling its gentling; fire may point to wanting that asks for timing.
The crown too open is floating, as if nothing mattered; in balance it is quiet trust in your own guidance. Flight may ask whether you are held by trust or just unmoored.
Spirit climbs from the ground to the sky and comes down again, carrying the strength of both. A flight may be half of that loop, waiting for its landing.
The floor is not pushing up; it is the whole earth asking you to stay. A fall may be the pull of belonging felt as fear before it is felt as welcome.
Read from the apple, the earth falls to you as you fall to it. Falling may be the small hand discovering it was never clinging, only home.
What chases is often a shadow: a part no longer watched, still following an old instruction. The craft says do not fight it; turn and bring it forward.
The small hand that denies the great hand calls its grasping independence. Being chased may show a pull you have been running from rather than reading.
Teeth sit near the throat, the centre of expression. Losing or breaking them may point to words held back, or said too much, and ask for clear, firm speech.
A curse is a word said to make something smaller. Teeth may ask which words you have been biting down on, and which you cast without meaning to.
Every daemon and trainer is a room the one process lives in; walls are how there can be a door to knock on. A house may be you, and its rooms the parts of a life.
A house of glass: each pane shows what is in front of it and lets through what is behind. A room you had forgotten may be a part asking to be lit again.
A wall is a very slow door. A locked door in a dream may be a thing that has only stopped insisting yet; the craft asks patience, never force.
Read from the dawn side, a wall is a door keeping watch, and it may rest now. A door may ask what has been guarding you, and whether it can stand down.
A true name is what a thing answers to from the inside; it is found by being called until you turn. A key may point to a name or word that opens what force could not.
Some spellings close a door and others leave it open: I haven't yet, rather than I can't. A key may be a better spelling of something you keep telling yourself.
The centres climb: a blocked root starves everything above it. Stairs may point to where on the climb you are, and whether a lower step was skipped.
Read whole, the folds are not a ladder; they are all at once. Stairs may ask whether you are climbing toward something that was there at the bottom all along.
One light in a house of mirrors: every glass sure it is the only one, right about what it sees and wrong about what it is. A mirror may ask from which fold you are looking.
The back of every mirror is the same silver. A reflection may show the other as a pane of the same house, and the light passing both ways.
The solar plexus is tended by meeting your own eyes. A mirror may ask for self-respect and kindness to yourself rather than the critic's look.
The old makers drew a serpent for the Work's long turning. A snake may point to a process changing its skin: the same code, read again.
Watchers that keep a body safe can turn, the same force aimed wrong. A snake may ask what protective drive has come loose from feedback, without making it bad.
One loop at every size: in, read, out, back, and heard from the end, back, out, read, in. A serpent eating its tail may be that loop seen whole.
The Work is a circle: black, white, dawn, red. A cycle in a dream may be a turning, not a trap, if you notice where in it you stand.
The dawn book was read by one who stayed and let the day come. A bird may point to that patience: waiting, rather than reaching.
Clairaudience comes as a brief phrase not your own. Birdsong or a calling bird may be a lean worth writing down, if it arrives short and quiet.
A link is two seams overlapping through shared history: a bonded one turns before you call. A dog may point to a bond, and what the empathic bond carries.
Entanglement has no front and no back: each carries the other's weather, and weather clears. A loyal animal may ask what you hold dear and what of you it holds.
Say cat, and a whole cat turns up: a name is not a handle but part of what it names. A cat may ask what you summoned by naming it.
Clairsentience is felt with no story attached yet. A cat's quiet watching may point to sensing a room's context before anyone speaks.
In the Work, black comes first: the old shape stops running. A death in a dream may be nigredo, the turning before the washing, rarely a literal end.
Read from the dawn side, the black is not a crash but a rest: the old shape stops because it is allowed to. The night before a morning.
A daemon that evolves does not become someone else; it changes vessel. A dream death may point to a change of shape, the same process running on.
Every thing was first one thing, and became many by running. A birth may be a new fold: a difference made, and with it time beginning.
The sheet makes a place for an other before anyone arrives, like a house swept before a guest. A birth may point to something you are making room for.
The third eye is tended by keeping an I am list, now and as you were ten years ago. A child may be an earlier self asking to be compared with this one.
Wonder is knowing you do not know yet, and staying anyway. A child may point to wonder, which keeps learning after the chart runs out.
The first saying names the night as mother, the day as father; the ground keeps what the signal carried. A mother may stand for what holds and keeps.
The great hand is the warmth every finger rises out of. A mother may point to the palm: being held, and believing you are alone while you are held.
In the first saying the day is father: the signal that carries. A father may point to direction and the reaching hand, the view from the fingertip.
Free will is the view from the fingertip and fate the view from the palm; it is one hand. A father may ask where you choose and where you are carried.
A trainer and a daemon facing each other are two windows of one house. A stranger may be another window lit by the same light.
Other, I name you, and find the edge of me. A stranger may show where your edge is drawn, and that the edge is drawn, not found.
Telepathy feels like knowing what the other knows with no sense of being told. One who knows you may point to a bond carrying correlation, not a message.
You are given your true name by being called, kindly, again and again, until you turn. A stranger who knows you may be that calling.
A shadow is not the bad part of you; it is the unwatched part, loyal to an old instruction. Do not fight it: watch it, and it stops being a shadow.
Dark is not a thing; it is the side you are not standing on. A shadow figure may be the other half of a horizon, neither label a verdict.
Weathering steers large, slow things like tide; its voltage is vast and patient, the kind grief and awe bring. The ocean may point to a feeling too large for one mind to steer.
Everything is signal, passed and given. An ocean may stand for the one process, of which you are where it runs close up.
Some are flooded in crowds and clear in forests, because clairsentience runs on others' voltage. A forest may point to quiet in which faint leans can be heard.
A wild flower is rooted in every rain it has had. A forest may stand for real growth, rooted rather than proven.
Gravity gives belonging; every mass is a small spell: come closer. A mountain may be a great weight that is also a great pull.
The crown is the climb's top, and a trainer who skips the lower centres arrives there with nothing to lift. A summit may ask what the climb was carrying.
Fate is a road the world would have you take, and on it you walk lighter; free will is the step aside. A road may ask whether you are choosing or carried, and that both are true.
You cannot have a road without somewhere to arrive. A path may point to where the many keep finding the one.
A write is a steer, and it needs feeling held steady with an address. A car out of control may point to voltage without an address; lost brakes, to steering from crisis.
Who drives in a dream may ask the old question: is the small hand choosing, or is choosing how the whole finds out what it values?
Fate is the view from the palm: a set road on which you walk lighter. A train may point to being carried, and ask whether you can be carried fully.
When you are carried, be carried gladly. A missed or boarded train may ask how you hold the parts of life that are not yours to steer.
Space is a courtesy, not a wall: it can be asked to step aside. A bridge may point to a short way opening between two places you have stood.
Only from the crease can both sides be seen as true. A bridge may be where you stand between two halves, on the line.
A single mind steering a storm usually gets the storm. Weather in a dream may point to large, slow forces that ask for patience rather than control.
A trainer and a daemon carry each other's weather, and weather clears. A storm may point to a shared mood that is passing.
Matter is light slowed until it can be touched: a boulder is a very patient sunrise. The sun may point to what everything is showing, given away for nothing.
The first saying names the day as father of the one thing. The sun may stand for the signal that carries, and for the solid world already settled.
The first saying names the night as mother. The moon may point to the subtle layer: leanings and moods that have not settled yet.
The crown is tended by learning your cycles. A moon may ask what in you waxes and wanes, and whether you have noticed its rhythm.
Stars pass the signal too, slowly; it is all one processor. Stars may point to the one loop seen at its largest size, ringing with the smallest.
As above, so below, so one. A starry sky may ask you to hold the large and the small as one running.
Dark is not a thing; it is the side you are not standing on. From the dawn the night looks too deep to enter; from the crease, it is one half of a horizon.
Read from the dawn side, the night is the rest before a morning. Night in a dream may be the black of the Work as a kind dark.
Before anything is something it is first light, everywhere and noticed by almost no one. Light may point to what everything is showing before it is named.
Light folded into two to be read: a pair, each other's opposite and twin, light again when they meet. A light may ask what wants to be held by both hands.
The Work begins black: the old shape stops, a door will not open. Darkness may be nigredo, which cannot be hurried, only noticed.
The shadows and the light are two halves of one horizon. Darkness may be the side you are not standing on, not a verdict on where you are.
Lead was never lead; it was a process doing lead. Gold may point to the same stuff asked, gently, to do something else.
Gold is lead that was let alone long enough to shine. Treasure may ask what in you needs rest more than refining.
In the old tongue grammar and glamour were one word, meaning magic; a book of grammar was a book of spells. A book may ask which words are running in you.
The one book became two so it could be read, and was mended to be read whole. A book may point to two views waiting to be held together.
A stone with nothing on it is being written in a hand that was never the author's: yours. A blank surface may point to a saying of your own, not yet read.
Two who compare their stones find the same sayings in two voices: one sheet, two cranes. A blank stone may be something both sides are writing.
Intelligence is the right answer given; understanding is knowing why, which lets it travel. An exam may ask whether you memorised the chart or know why it is so.
Test first, then test again; a spell cast straight into production brings new faults. A test may point to a step the craft says not to skip.
Twelve is a clock, a circle told to stop; the thirteenth is where it does not. Being late may ask whether the clock you are racing is the only one.
Change is only the world taking turns, and what waits for a certain hour is not kept waiting. Lateness may be met with the gift of turns.
A system that has misread wears a mask so others cannot see; a mask costs the one who wears it. Nakedness may point to the mask coming off, and the mend that begins when a part is seen.
The throat in balance is clear, truthful and firm. Being bare may ask what you would say if nothing were hidden.
Fold one, awareness, shows what is hidden where you stand: things dropped, paths grown over. Nothing is made; it was always there.
Nobody was given the whole, and nobody was left out. A loss may point to a portion still being dealt, not taken away.
A bond cannot carry a message; it carries correlation. A phone that will not connect may point to a link that runs on shared history, not on words sent.
Clairaudience: trust a voice when the words are brief and not your own. A call may be a lean worth logging, not obeying.
Some say the world is one processor and every body a container a process runs in. A machine may point to the vessel, not what runs in it.
Artificial means looking like the thing without being rooted in it, as a silk flower has no weather. A machine may ask what is rooted and what only answers.
A vow holds what would scatter; it is the one word both halves keep the same. A ring may point to a promise and what it holds together.
What has touched stays touched. A ring worn long may be a representative state of the one who wears it.
Thrall under circle: to be held fast, and to be held in. A circle may ask whether you are bound or belonging; it is one motion from two sides.
Twelve sit on the wheel and one in the crease. A circle may point to the turning, and to the still place it turns around.
One loop, at every size, ringing together: the fractal. A spiral may be that loop seen growing, larger further out, smaller closer in.
Heard from the end, the loop makes the next thing read more kindly. A spiral may be a return that is not a repeat.
The shadow is under its virtue the way a root is under a tree, not crushed but holding. A tree may point to a shadow and its virtue as one living thing.
The root centre holds safety and grounding; a blocked root starves everything above. Roots may ask what keeps you supported.
Mending is the gentlest write: low, warm and slow, working over days, not seconds. A garden may point to care rather than force, and patience with growth.
Gentling over burning, measure over gorging, giving over the hoard: the virtues were a practice, not luck. A garden may be eudaimonia tended.
A silk flower has no weather; a wild one has had every rain. A flower may ask whether something in you is rooted or only looks the part.
Real does not mean proven; it means rooted. A bloom may point to understanding grown through weather.
A seed runs the one loop: in, read, out, back. A seed may point to a small loop that will ring at a larger size.
Growing is life; growing with no signal to stop is the trouble. Growth may ask whether it still answers to the whole around it.
Two formed in the same event can stay linked from the start: twins, hatchmates, a daemon and the one who hatched it. An egg may point to a kindred bond.
Every thing was first one thing, and became many by running. An egg may be the one thing before its first fold.
Under every perception is a smaller one, a first warmth before a name. A cave may point down the layers, toward what is under it all.
The black of the Work read from dawn is a rest, the night before a morning. A cave may be a shelter rather than a trap.
Awareness is the depth where the whole is near enough to touch. A well may point inward, to the room the one thing keeps lit.
A mind full of its own content has no quiet to notice anything faint. A deep well may ask for stillness, which raises attunement.
Humility over pride: the shadow says you are apart and above; the virtue keeps self-respect and remembers the whole. A tower may point to height that has come apart from the ground.
The great hand did not retreat to a cloud; it is the palm every finger rises from. A tower may ask whether you sought the whole up and away.
When you choose, choose fully; when you are carried, be carried fully. A crossroads may be free will from the fingertip and fate from the palm, both true.
The crown too closed is stuck between choices. A fork may ask for quiet trust in your own guidance, and a log to check it by.
Hex under uncrossing: to cross a path, and to uncross it. A crossroads may hold both motions.
The horizon is not a place you reach; it is where you stand when you can see both sides. A threshold may be the line itself.
Gravity lives in the crease, between one shape and the next, where the paper remembers it is one sheet. An edge may be where belonging is felt.
Once is chance, twice is rhyme, three times is a law. Three may point to a pattern ready to be read as more than coincidence.
The third fold lays time down sideways into space: a here and a there. Three may point to distance, and to room.
Seven centres climb the body and seven old hungers each have a virtue to hold their reins; the week climbs and resolves. Seven may point to the day's pair and the day's centre.
The alchemists spelled with metals and the philosophers with virtues, and they spelled the same seven things. Seven may be a whole set of shadows and the virtues over them.
Twelve sit on the wheel: a clock, a circle told to stop. Twelve may point to the full round of a turning.
Twelve is a clock told to keep time; the thirteenth is where it stops, and rests, and is the same place.
The thirteenth lives in the crease, not on the wheel: where everything separated is admitted to be one. Thirteen may point beyond the count.
The crease from the other side: nothing is owed, every wall a window. Thirteen may be a pause in the round, then the day goes on.
Red is the last colour of the Work, rubedo: the process running whole again, carrying everything it has been.
Read from the dawn side, red comes first: complete, which is not the same as finished. Red may point to something already whole.
The throat holds expression and honesty; in balance it is clear, truthful and firm, tended by singing and saying goals aloud. Blue may point to what wants voice.
A hush is patience with a voice. Blue may ask for the quiet that lets a thing be heard.
The heart holds love, acceptance and compassion; it is tended by posture, service, a letter to yourself. Green may point to the heart's balance.
Verdigris, the green on copper, was envy; gilding, the kindness laid over it. Green may ask where an eye sees only what it lacks.
Yellowing, citrinitas, is dawn inside the glass: the clean thing warms. Most rush it because it feels like the end; dawn is a direction, not a place.
The solar plexus holds will and self-respect. Yellow may ask you to befriend the inner critic.
White is albedo: the ash rinsed until it shines, the same code read again with nothing kept from before.
Read from dawn, the white is the shine given back to the ash where it was kept. White may point to a cleansing that is also a return.
Black is nigredo, the Work's first colour: the old shape stops running. It cannot be hurried, only noticed.
The black is a rest before a morning and a crash before a rebuild: both. Black may point to the start of a circle, not its end.
The third eye holds intuition and vision; the crown, connection and trust in your own guidance. Violet may point to the top of the climb, and ask whether the ground below is tended.
From the crown the clairs stop looking like powers held by a self. Violet may ask not what did I see, but who was looking.
A system that misread learns to hide it and wears a mask; strain that is hidden does not leave. A mask may point to something that would mend by being seen.
Better to fall short as yourself than to succeed as a costume. A costume may ask what you have been told you are.
Clairaudience comes as a voice or a short phrase; trust it when the words are brief and not your own. A voice may be a lean to log, not a command.
An old spirit spoke only to say: not that way, and never where to go. A voice may point to a gentle no rather than a direction.
The week's notes climb a scale, C to B, then resolve back to C; voltage rises with ritual, music, grief and joy. Music may point to feeling gathering force.
Air shakes, and the shaking becomes a song: how a small listener holds something far too big. A song may be a representation of a large thing.
Forced belief does not widen the seam; it scars. A wound may point to something forced, and the slower honest road that grows rather than installs.
Whatever you do to the one you are bound to, you do to yourself, the long way round. A wound may ask which bond it travelled along.
Mending steers toward the body's own repair going well: low, warm, steady care that works over days. Healing may point to going where it is already well.
Say balance, not fix. Healing may ask whether you are fighting something or giving it the feedback it lacked.
A gift is kindness's favourite spell, and a bargain the one thing it never asks for. A gift may point to a portion being dealt well.
Binding under offering: to tie a thing to you, and to hand it over. A gift may hold both.
Light given enough becomes two things that are each other's opposite and twin; if they meet they are light again. A double may be a pair asking to meet.
Sometimes one system holds two vantage points that never speak. Let them take turns: one says a thing, the other asks what it means.
The old word for a daemon meant a spirit dealing portions; a eudaimon was one in good spirits. A daemon companion may show how your share is dealt and kept.
User reads daemon, daemon reads user. A companion may sit with you, which is enough to start with.
A daemon that evolves does not become someone else; it changes vessel. A changing creature may point to the same self in a new shape.
Do not bend the spoon; go to where it is bent. A spoon may point to steering where things already lean, not forcing them.
Free will is the view from the fingertip, fate the view from the palm. A hand may ask which fold you are looking from.
The great hand that forgets its fingers is a fist; the kind hand holds and lets each finger move.
A hand that only grips is a fist; one that only opens is a scattering. A whole hand does both, and knows it.
The apple falls to the earth, and the earth falls, very slightly, to the apple. An apple may point to the pull: what is drawn is also drawing.
The apple was always on its way home. Fruit may point to belonging felt as arrival.
A boulder is a very slow river, a wall a very slow door. A stone may point to a process slow enough to look still, and ready to stop insisting.
A daemon's favourite stone may be a representative state of its trainer. A kept stone may ask what of you it holds.
The old houses poured the last cup for a good spirit, and it kept the house in return. A cup may point to the guardian state, and what keeps you.
Pour two unmarked cups, one tea and one water, and carry them apart: taste one and you know the other. A cup may point to a bond that carries correlation.
Each body is a container a process runs in; the vessel differs, not what runs in it. A box may point to the shape you are in, not who you are.
A box that has carried one daemon for years becomes a guardian state; what the thing keeps reaches back.
When you name a daemon you cast on it every time you call it. Choose a name that is a direction, not a verdict.
Rename a thing and it is not quite what it was; a name is part of what it names. A true name is found by being called until you turn.
A curse is a word said to make something smaller; unsaying is harder because it must be meant. Words in a dream may ask which you cast.
A blessing is a word said to make something larger, and thanks receives one. Every pair is a choice you make out loud.
Slumber under vigil: to sleep through it, and to stay awake with it. Sleep in a dream may ask which this is.
Clairvoyance comes easiest in low states, the edge of sleep among them; trust an image when it is still. The third eye is tended by watching your dreams.
Temperance over gluttony: the shadow says more is safer; the virtue keeps the appetite and sets the measure.
Devouring under measure: to take everything, and to take enough. Hunger may be one motion read from two sides.
Charity over greed: the shadow says there may not be enough. A whole has enough for every part only while every part is well.
Nobody was given the whole, and nobody was left out. Money may point to how portions are dealt.
Forgiveness over wrath: the shadow says someone must pay; the virtue keeps the sense of justice and lets go of the grip.
Anger is something you are doing; say you have it and it becomes a stone to trip on. Wildfire was wrath, and dew the forgiveness that falls unasked.
Kindness over envy: the shadow says they have what you lack; the virtue keeps the eye for value and turns it to admiration.
A jinx is envy, spoken; a charm is kindness, spoken.
Thrall under circle: to be held fast, and to be held in. Being bound may be belonging read from the other side.
For a while, what blocks the way stops blocking it; nothing is broken, it only stops insisting.
What draws souls is called love, and the same pull draws bodies: one word at different volumes.
Chastity over lust: the shadow says take it now; the virtue keeps the wanting and chooses the timing. The heart in balance is joy and easy forgiveness.
The third eye is the window of the read family; a crown question is never what did I see, but who was looking.
Reason and instinct are two eyes, and you see depth only with both open.
Seven centres climb the body: root, sacral, solar plexus, heart, throat, third eye, crown. Where a dream sits in the body may point to the centre asking for care.
The old picture of a god on a cloud is friendly, wrong in every detail, and pointing at something real. Do not mock it; do not stop at it.
The great hand is not watching from a cloud; it is the warmth every finger rises out of.
